newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tsang sees no short-term change in Land Fund mgt.
newsitem.headline: Tsang sees no short-term change in Land Fund mgt.

text.p: Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said he saw no short-term change in the management of Hong Kong's Land Fund, but he expected to review the government's highly-conservative management of the Exchange Fund.
"In the short term I am not going to make any changes because I have sufficient money, as you know, in my bank account without dipping my hand into the Land Fund," Tsang told Reuters.

The US$19 billion Land Fund, made up of government property sales revenues, was established to counter fears that Britain would scoop Hong Kong's coffers when it hands back the territory to China at midnight on June 30.
The Land Fund is being managed through a different investment strategy from the Exchange Fund, which holds most of Hong Kong's US$63.8 billion in foreign exchange reserves.
"We will be looking at the investment strategy for the Land Fund and also the strategy for the Exchange Fund for that matter because we are now going through a different phase," Tsang said.
The imminent transfer to Chinese rule will allow Hong Kong's money managers to adopt a slightly less risk-averse investment strategy, he said.
"We are now going through a different phase with the transition out of the way and we can look at whether we can aim at a higher return than we have before," Tsang said.

"We have been applying a highly conservative investment strategy simply because we are going through a political transition," he said. "When 1997 is no longer an issue that should be the time for us to look at what to do with that sum of money."

Responding to reports that some of the Land Fund could be invested in infrastructure projects in southern China, Tsang issued a forceful reminder that approval of Hong Kong's legislature would be required before any money could be invested outside the territory.
